title: Taking the Cell Apart, Then Rebuilding It

scenes.tts: Can a process run without the cell around it? Before eighteen ninety-seven, many held that fermentation was tied to living yeast. Yeast cells were thought too small to be broken open. Vitalists held that the chemistry of life was inseparable from the intact cell. A cell has many parts. Which does a process need, and which are enough?

scenes.visual: A yeast cell holds six boxes marked ?, fermentation tethered to it; a red cross: too small to break open; the ring thickens: inseparable; boxes flash; needed? enough?

scenes.tts: Buchner broke the cells. He ground brewer's yeast with quartz sand and diatomite, then squeezed it in a hydraulic press. A thousand grams of yeast gave about five hundred C C of juice. That juice fermented sugar with no living cells. Next, show the activity runs in the crude extract, and give it a number.

That juice fermented sugar with no living cells. Next, show the activity runs in the crude extract, and give it a number.

scenes.visual: Cells in a mortar are ground to fragments; pressed in canvas, juice drips into a tube; the tube grows, bubbles rise; a gauge fills and is read as a number.

scenes.tts: Next, split the extract. A column can do it. In a lysate of reticulocytes, one fraction does not bind the column: Fraction 1. The other is washed off with high salt: Fraction 2. Neither supports A T P dependent protein breakdown alone. Combined, they restore that activity.

scenes.visual: Crude extract tube; a column separates blue and orange dots into Fraction 1 and 2; each alone has an empty gauge; together the gauge fills.

scenes.tts: Now test one part at a time. Remove one protein with an antibody, and the activity is lost. Add the pure protein back, and it returns. The last test is to rebuild. Mix only purified parts: for E. coli mismatch repair, eight proteins, with A T P and D N T Ps. If the reaction runs, those parts are enough.

scenes.visual: One tube and gauge: an antibody pulls the purple protein out, the gauge drops, pure protein returns it; then ten purified parts are mixed in an empty tube and the gauge fills.

scenes.tts: Cytosol from growing cells plus D A T P starts parts of the apoptotic program. Fractionation gave a fifteen kilodalton protein, which proved to be cytochrome c. Immunodepleting it diminished the activity. Adding cytochrome c back restored it. Diminished when removed, restored when added back: the protein is needed.
scenes.narration: Cytosol from growing cells plus dATP starts parts of the apoptotic program. Fractionation gave a 15 kDa protein, which proved to be cytochrome c. Immunodepleting it diminished the activity. Adding cytochrome c back restored it. Diminished when removed, restored when added back: the protein is needed.

scenes.visual: Three idealised bars (marked example): tall, low after immunodepletion, tall again with cytochrome c added back; a chip 15 kDa protein turns into cytochrome c; arrows read the pattern.

scenes.tts: Two things can mislead. A few living cells might survive in the juice. They were too few: a control with ten times as many cells as the juice held gave no fermentation. Killed dried yeast, called zymin, still fermented. Second, how you prepare an extract changes what it contains. In Wang's system, sucrose added to stabilize mitochondria diminished the apoptotic activity. Intact mitochondria likely held back the cytochrome c that was part of it.

scenes.visual: Two control panels with gauges (ten times the cells, killed yeast); then two cytosol tubes, without and with sucrose, mitochondria and purple cytochrome c.

scenes.tts: In the nineteen fifties, Sutherland and Rall found that a hormone response survived breaking the cells. It split into a membrane step and a soluble step. That needed broken cells. In nineteen sixty-one, Nirenberg and Matthaei added synthetic poly U, a template no cell would take up, to an E. coli extract. It made polyphenylalanine, the first codon assignment.

scenes.visual: Sutherland and Rall: the response splits into an orange membrane step and a blue soluble step. Nirenberg and Matthaei: poly-U added to an extract, polyphenylalanine appears.

scenes.tts: In the late nineteen seventies, Hershko and colleagues combined fractions of reticulocyte lysate. Neither fraction alone gave A T P dependent protein breakdown. Together they restored it. Only a tube lets fractions be combined and recombined. In nineteen eighty-nine, Murray and Kirschner made frog egg extracts cycle. Destroying their messenger R N A arrested them in interphase. Adding cyclin messenger R N A restored the cycles. A tube shows what the parts can do, not that the cell uses them that way. A separate experiment is needed, such as a mutant or a cell test.

Only a tube lets fractions be combined and recombined. In 1989, Murray and Kirschner made frog egg extracts cycle. Destroying their messenger RNA arrested them in interphase. Adding cyclin messenger RNA restored the cycles. A tube shows what the parts can do, not that the cell uses them that way. A separate experiment is needed, such as a mutant or a cell test.
